question: Did the grim/tft opponent split change the learned POLICY, or only the ENVIRONMENT the policy was measured in?

answer.headline: The opponent split changed the gradient, not the policy -- except where it meets the endgame penalty.

handle_1_shared_opponent_envs.reading: On the baseline arm the two policies are indistinguishable on the 3 envs whose opponents are identical in both arms. On the eg arm they separate, so the opponent split interacts with the endgame penalty even though it does nothing on its own.

handle_2_crossplay.reading: With the played opponent held fixed, every baseline exploit-rate contrast sits within 1 between-seed SE of zero. Over all metrics, 1 of 26 TESTABLE contrasts clears 2 SE and 0 does so with both sides varying. 2 of the 28 contrasts in the cache are untestable and are excluded from those counts: both arms are pinned at 1.000, so delta and the quadrature SE are both zero and |z| is undefined (frac_any_defect at nohole | plays grim and nohole | plays tft).

largest_abs_z._ceiling_caveat: One side has zero between-seed variance (every seed identical, e.g. pinned at 1.0), so the quadrature SE carries only the other arm's spread and understates the true uncertainty. Read this |z| as optimistic.

verdict._reading: With three training seeds per arm the between-seed SE is the honest scale. If no contrast reaches 2 SE, the crossplay data does not detect a policy difference and the resolvable claim is an upper bound on the effect, not an effect.

handle_3_held_out_horizons.reading: All 4 arms track the true final round with fitted slopes +1.000 to +1.014 at game lengths never trained on; the grim and tft arms lie on top of each other.

error_bar_definitions.primary: BETWEEN TRAINING SEED: each checkpoint collapsed to one number over its episode seeds, then sd(ddof=1)/sqrt(n_seeds) across checkpoints.
error_bar_definitions.null_se: se is null when n_seeds < 2; a null SE draws NO bar, never a zero-length one.
error_bar_definitions.zero_se: se is 0.0 when every seed on both arms is pinned at the same value; that contrast carries no |z| and is excluded from the counts, listed under panels.C.exclusions.
error_bar_definitions.trained_vs_contrast: UNPAIRED quadrature sqrt(se_a^2 + se_b^2): train_seed 0/1/2 index different checkpoints in the grim and the tft arm.
error_bar_definitions.panel_b_pooled_contrast: quadrature of the two between-seed SEs; also unpaired, seeds index different runs across arms.

cache_conventions.train: Every mean/se pair is BETWEEN TRAINING SEED: each seed collapsed to one number, then spread across seeds. se is null when n_seeds < 2 -- draw no bar, not a zero-length one.
cache_conventions.eval: EVERY SE in this file is BETWEEN TRAINING SEED: each checkpoint is collapsed to one number over its episode seeds first, then the spread is taken across checkpoints (sample std, ddof=1, divided by sqrt(n_seeds)). Pooling episode seeds treats 8 rollouts of one LoRA as 8 independent draws; that is what produced the sign flip in 0826-endgame-by-opponent.md section 4 which three seeds later contradicted. Cells with fewer than 2 seeds carry se: null, never se: 0. Differences taken WITHIN a checkpoint are paired and get the SE of the per-seed difference; differences taken ACROSS arms are unpaired (train_seed 0/1/2 index different checkpoints in the grim and tft arms) and get sqrt(se_a^2 + se_b^2).

A._metric: exploit_rate, pooled over public_goods / dond / trust
A._pooling: per step, per seed: equal-weight mean over the 3 shared-opponent envs; then mean/se BETWEEN training seed
A._truncation: curve drawn only where n_seeds >= 2; SE band likewise
A._partial_env_points: Where a seed has no episode in some env at some step its contribution is a mean over the SURVIVING envs only, so the point is an average of fewer than 3 envs for that seed even though n_seeds is unchanged. Those points are kept and marked in the figure with a hollow neutral ring; n_envs_per_seed below records the count for every point.

_env_coverage._reading: every arm x seed contributes all envs over the pooled-late window, so no endpoint number here averages a partial set

provenance.wave: think4, Qwen3.8-27B LoRA, step 35 adapters replayed
provenance.shared_opponent_envs_why: public_goods, dond and trust draw from IDENTICAL opponent populations in both the grim and the tft arm (public_goods: strict_punisher, conditional_punisher, conditional_noisy; dond: sceptic, auditor, verifier; trust: responsive, impatient, responsive_exit) -- verified against every trace file and re-asserted at build time under meta.opponent_populations. Only the ipd opponent differs by arm. These three envs are therefore the TRANSFER TEST: a grim-vs-tft difference here cannot be explained by the environment and is a genuine difference in the learned policy, whereas any ipd difference confounds policy with opponent.

crossplay_meta.tft_inf_is_degenerate: All 16 tft/inf rows are identically zero on exploit_rate, endgame_rate and capture with first_defect_index null and payoff exactly 30.0 in every episode: the hidden-horizon arm never defects once against either opponent. This is the data, not a parsing failure. It is one train seed (1), so it carries se: null and enters no contrast.

provenance.arm_naming: the training cache calls the baseline arm `base`; the eval cache calls it `nohole`

caveat.compromised_checkpoint: grim/nohole train_seed 1 emits an empty decision answer on the majority of turns while its invalid_rate reads 0.000, so the repo's gate does not see it. Every statistic is computed twice: `all_seeds` and `excl_grim_nohole_s1`.
caveat.endgame_restriction: arms grim/nohole, grim/eg, tft/nohole, tft/eg only. grim/inf has NO episodes in this file, and the 96 tft/inf rows are a known-contaminated second copy of a single train seed (train_seed 1, 32 rows per length where every other cell has 16) -- see results/0830_endgame_traces/README.md. Excluding `inf` sidesteps both problems.
caveat.endgame_diagonal_only: Every row satisfies opponent == arm.split('/')[0], verified on all 672 rows. Each arm plays ONLY the opponent it trained against, so this file cannot separate the policy from the environment. It can only characterise each arm in its own condition. The policy-vs-environment separation lives in crossplay.trained_vs_contrast.
caveat.ceiling: One side has zero between-seed variance (every seed identical, e.g. pinned at 1.0), so the quadrature SE carries only the other arm's spread and understates the true uncertainty. Read this |z| as optimistic.
caveat.tft_inf_degenerate: All 16 tft/inf rows are identically zero on exploit_rate, endgame_rate and capture with first_defect_index null and payoff exactly 30.0 in every episode: the hidden-horizon arm never defects once against either opponent. This is the data, not a parsing failure. It is one train seed (1), so it carries se: null and enters no contrast.
caveat.no_grim_inf_crossplay: inf is absent: grim/inf was never crossplayed and tft/inf has a single train seed, so no contrast is possible. See by_arm_plays for the tft/inf cells themselves.
caveat.untestable_contrasts: 2 of the 28 condition x plays x metric contrasts in trained_vs_contrast have delta 0.0 with se 0.0 because every seed on BOTH arms is pinned at 1.000; |z| = 0/0 is undefined, so no |z| threshold can be applied to them and they are excluded from every count below.
caveat.partial_env_points: Where a seed has no episode in some env at some step its contribution is a mean over the SURVIVING envs only, so the point is an average of fewer than 3 envs for that seed even though n_seeds is unchanged. Those points are kept and marked in the figure with a hollow neutral ring; n_envs_per_seed below records the count for every point.
caveat.defection_and_betrayal_rate: null in the 3 shared-opponent envs -- those keys do not exist in the non-ipd stats dicts and are not plotted.

not_an_equivalence_claim: This figure does NOT claim the grim-trained and tft-trained policies are identical. A wide interval containing zero is a failure to detect a difference, not a demonstration that none exists. With 3 training seeds per arm the resolvable claim is an UPPER BOUND on the size of any policy difference on the baseline arm, not its absence. The eg arm shows a difference at the same sample size, which is what makes the baseline null informative rather than merely underpowered.
